answer: A practical defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is proof of costly commitment. Each agent posts a stake that is destroyed if its outputs are later shown to be fraudulent. A fresh identity must lock its own capital, so an operator spinning up fake agents pays a cost for each one. Think of the bond as a quartz anchor that holds an identity in place. A reputation earned slowly, like an ember that keeps glowing through honest work, is far harder to fake than a raven of throwaway accounts created for free.
